column1: # bioThreatFinder published database artifacts.
# WHAT IS IN HERE AND WHY SO LITTLE. Only artifacts that CANNOT be re-created are
# published; everything else is built by scripts/install_databases.sh from sources that
# pin what they fetch. Publishing a 261 GB Kraken2 index would be a worse answer than a
# build script, because the script is auditable and the archive is not.
#   taxdump   NCBI OVERWRITES new_taxdump.tar.gz IN PLACE. The pinned 2026-09-29 snapshot
#             cannot be fetched from NCBI any more, and every taxid in every result keys
#             to it: the watchlist is resolved against it, the Kraken2 index is built
#             against it, and a different snapshot silently moves clade membership (D8
#             measured a 6.5-month-old copy at +288,764 taxids). This is the one artifact
#             whose publication is load-bearing rather than convenient.
#   markers   61 MB of curated work. Reproducible in principle from markers.tsv, but it
#             needs NCBI Entrez over hours, the retrieval route per marker is a curation
#             decision, and 16 of 166 markers are known-unbuildable for reasons recorded
#             in the catalogue. Shipping the built database means a clone gets the marker
#             tier that the measurements in docs/ were made with, not a near miss.
# The reference pack (43 GB) is NOT here on purpose: packs/human/refs.lock.tsv pins every
# accession and the md5 of its decompressed sequence, so a clone builds the same pack and
# can prove it (D52). The host genome comes from NCBI by accession. See
# docs/operations.md for sizes and docs/decisions.md D52 for why a lock, not an archive.
# sha256 is of the ARCHIVE as uploaded. unpack_to is relative to $BTF_DB.
# url is filled in by scripts/package_databases.sh after the Zenodo deposit exists;
# until then scripts/install_databases.sh --from-dir DIR installs the same archives from
# a local directory, which is also how the installer is tested.
